title: From Phishing to LLMjacking: Threat Actors Targeting Cloud Billing Accounts for LLM Usage
description: Threat actors are conducting phishing campaigns targeting Google Cloud Platform (GCP) environments by using sponsored search ads to steal privileged user credentials. They disable security controls, create service accounts with Gemini API access, and link attacker-controlled external projects to victim billing accounts. This enables unauthorized large-scale AI workload execution, causing significant unexpected charges within 24-48 hours. The attackers use evasion techniques such as geographic IP blending and demoting legitimate administrators to avoid detection and remediation.
aiSummary: This campaign involves threat actors targeting GCP environments through phishing attacks delivered via sponsored search ads. After compromising privileged credentials through fake login pages, attackers manipulate organizational policies to disable security guardrails. They create service accounts with access to the Gemini API and invite external attacker-controlled accounts, assigning them administrative billing roles. By linking their external GCP projects to victim billing accounts, attackers execute large-scale AI workloads that generate unauthorized charges ranging from tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars within 1-2 days. The campaign employs evasion tactics including geographic IP blending and demoting legitimate administrators to hinder detection and response efforts.
aiImpact: Victims suffer unauthorized financial charges on their cloud billing accounts due to attacker-driven AI workload execution. Security controls are disabled, increasing exposure to further compromise. The attackers' ability to hide activity and demote legitimate administrators complicates detection and remediation, potentially leading to prolonged abuse and financial loss.
